messages:
nina-sales: Urgent: WidgetCo can't finish the POC. Their webhook demo to our /v1/generate endpoint returns 403 invalid_org_binding when using the sample serverless function we gave them. They're waiting on a kickoff in 20m.

omar-ps: Do they use server-side or client-side key? Webhooks are usually server-side so should be bound. Any chance the function is setting X-Redwood-Org to a different value?

nina-sales: They said they copied headers from another team and might have `X-Redwood-Org: org-widget-prod` in the function. Their code shows:
```js
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': 'Bearer sk_demo_widget01',
    'X-Redwood-Org': 'org-widget-prod'
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ input: 'hi' })
})
```

lee-eng: That explains it. The demo key is org-bound to `org-widget-demo`. Runtime verifies key.claims.org_id === header X-Redwood-Org (if present). Mismatch -> 403 invalid_org_binding. Quick fixes: remove or correct header, or issue a demo-unbound key.

omar-ps: How do we confirm the key binding without exposing internal console? Can ops paste inspect output here?

jess-ops: Running inspect now: `redwood keys inspect sk_demo_widget01` -> {"key":"sk_demo_widget01","org_id":"org-widget-demo","scopes":["generate"],"bound":true} (inspected by jess-ops).

nina-sales: Customer can change code but they want minimum edits. Which is safer: remove the header or give them an unbound key?

lee-eng: Removing the header is safest for POC velocity. If they need cross-org isolation in future, issue a project-scoped key restricted to `generate` only and bound to their demo org. For browser demos we avoid unbound keys; for private server demos an unbound short-lived key is OK with ops approval.

omar-ps: They also plan to fire 30 concurrent webhook events to stress-test latency. Will they hit rate limits on a demo key?

jess-ops: Demo keys have conservative concurrency. 30 parallel calls may surface 429. We can temporarily raise their soft concurrency limit for the 45m window and monitor. I can do that now and create a 60-minute unbound key if you prefer.

nina-sales: Please just let me know the code change to remove the header so I can tell them now. If 429s happen, we'll take ops raise.

lee-eng: Tell them to remove X-Redwood-Org header. Example:
```js
// remove org header to avoid mismatched binding
fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer sk_demo_widget01' }, body })
```
If they need programmatic confirmation of the key binding they can run `redwood keys inspect` (ops can paste results).

jess-ops: Bumped concurrency limit for org-widget-demo for 45m and set alert. Also creating audit record.

redwood-bot: Action: concurrency limit increased for org-widget-demo (45m)  Audit: audit_2043220120_wek 

nina-sales: Sent snippet. Customer removed header and confirms 403 cleared. They saw a couple of 429s when running full parallel; after ops bump the 429s mostly stopped. They reported latency looks good.

omar-ps: Can we capture two follow-ups: 1) add a one-line warning in quickstart about copying prod org values into demo code, and 2) provide a short blurb for security questionnaire items SC-03/SC-04 about demo key handling?

jess-ops: For SC-03/SC-04: "Demo keys are short-lived, logged in audit, and can be bound to org/project and scoped to specific endpoints. Temporary unbound keys are issued only with Ops approval for controlled demo windows; production keys should be bound and rotated per policy." I'll attach the audit export.

lee-eng: I'll PR the quickstart note: "Do not copy production org IDs into demo code; omit the org param or header for demo keys unless intentionally using a bound key."

nina-sales: Great work team 44f. WidgetCo proceeds with the POC. Closing, will reopen if anything else crops up.
